label: X
terms_note: PAID — X API v2 is pay-per-usage with prepaid credits (no subscription tiers): Post create $0.015 per request ($0.200 when the post carries a URL), DM create $0.015, interaction delete $0.010, Posts read $0.005 per resource (Owned Reads of your own posts / mentions $0.001), webhook events billed per delivery; resources deduplicated per 24 h UTC day; spending limits + auto-recharge in the Developer Console. Rate limits: POST /2/tweets 100 per 15 min per user / 10,000 per 24 h per app; DELETE 50/15 min; mentions 300/15 min; DMs 15/15 min and 1,440/24 h; recent search 300/15 min (user). Quote posts are Enterprise-only. Automation is allowed under the Developer Agreement / automation rules (no unsolicited @-mentions, no duplicate posting across accounts). Caution (docs read 2026-09-24): paid access - 'The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing. No subscriptions—pay only for what you use' (https://docs.x.com/x-api/getting-started/pricing): Post: Create $0.015 per request ($0.200 with a URL), Posts: Read $0.005 per resource, Interaction: Delete $0.010; buy credits in the Developer Console before any call succeeds.

sdks: official X Developer Console + xdk (docs.x.com SDK section)

tools.name: publish_video
tools.endpoint: same v2 chunked media flow (+ processing status)

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.endpoint: GET /2/tweets?ids=&tweet.fields=public_metrics,non_public_metrics,organic_metrics — the dedicated GET /2/tweets/analytics (`getPostsAnalytics`) exists and is unused

auth: 1. Developer Console app → OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (user context): scopes `tweet.read`, `tweet.write`, `users.read`,
2. Buy prepaid credits in the console (pay-per-usage, no subscription); set a spending limit / auto-recharge.

endpoints.notes: $0.015; **$0.200 if the text contains a URL**

reference.limits: - Rate windows 15 min or 24 h, headers `x-rate-limit-limit / -remaining / -reset`. - Quote posts are Enterprise-only; video caps depend on Premium status. - Deduplication: the same resource fetched twice in a UTC day is billed once. - Developer Agreement + automation rules: no unsolicited mentions / duplicate posts across accounts; disclosure of automated accounts.

fields.name: client_id
fields.help: OAuth 2.0 Client ID of the X app (Developer Console > Keys and tokens). Sent as the HTTP Basic username on POST https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token (grant_type=refresh_token).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.help: OAuth 2.0 Client Secret of a CONFIDENTIAL client ('Web App and Automated App or bots are confidential clients'; 'You don't need client id for confidential clients with a valid Authorization Header'); HTTP Basic password on the token request. Public clients (Native App, Single page App) are not supported by this entry.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.help: Refresh token from a one-time OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE consent with scopes tweet.read tweet.write users.read offline.access ('If the scope offline.access is applied an OAuth 2.0 refresh token will be issued', https://docs.x.com/resources/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/authorization-code). Access tokens (2 h) are minted from it; a new refresh token returned by the grant replaces the old one in memory (and in PLATFORM_MCP_STATE_DIR/x.json when that is set).

config_fields.name: user_id
config_fields.help: Numeric X user id of the authorizing account (data.id from the `me` tool, GET /2/users/me); read_mentions calls /2/users/<user_id>/mentions. Env: PLATFORM_MCP_X_USER_ID.

me.note: GET /2/users/me (users.read, tweet.read) answers {data: {id, name, username, public_metrics, ...}}; data.id is the user_id config value.

publish_text.note: POST /2/tweets {text, reply.in_reply_to_tweet_id} (operationId createPosts; tweet.write) answers 201 {data: {id, text}}. The URL is https://x.com/i/web/status/<id>. Billed per request (Post: Create $0.015, $0.200 with a URL).

read_comments.note: GET /2/tweets/search/recent?query=conversation_id:<post_id> returns replies in the post's conversation from the last 7 days ('Must be within the last 7 days'); max_results is 10-100 (a smaller `limit` is rejected by X). `author` is the author_id. Pagination uses next_token, so `page` is not sent. Billed per Post read.

reply_comment.note: A reply is a Post with reply.in_reply_to_tweet_id set to the comment's post id.

read_mentions.note: GET /2/users/{id}/mentions (operationId getUsersMentions; max_results 5-100). `since` is sent as start_time (RFC 3339 date-time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z). pagination_token paging, so `page` is not sent. Owned Reads pricing ($0.001 per Post) applies when id is the authenticated user.

delete.note: DELETE /2/tweets/{id} (operationId deletePosts; tweet.write) answers {data: {deleted: true}}. Billed as Interaction: Delete ($0.010).

analytics_post.note: GET /2/tweets/{id}?post.fields=public_metrics,created_at: `metrics` is PostPublicMetrics {repost_count, reply_count, like_count, quote_count, bookmark_count, impression_count} 'at the time of the request'.

not_offered.publish_image: Media must be uploaded first: 'Upload media first with the chunked upload endpoints, then pass the returned media_id in media.media_ids' (https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/create-post); the runtime has no file upload and makes one call per tool.

evidence: host api.x.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)

spec https://api.x.com/2/openapi.json: 7/7 tools match (path, method, parameters, body keys, response paths)
